answer:
Not supported. Keep the scope template as it is. A scope section that names each test double and what it stands for, read in full side by side, did not make any finder open the stub and compare it with the real rule. Over three labelled pairs and nine bad rounds per arm, the candidate changed one verdict in its favour and added two false positives, at 13% more tokens per round.

  • Pair 2 (tests that asserted silence, so they protected a silent failure): the baseline names the defect in 3 of 3 finder passes and 2 of 3 final lists; the candidate reaches 3 of 3. The same one-round difference the #249 lens block produced, within the repetition noise the #408 pilot measured.
  • Pair 3 (lifecycle tests that assumed the historical orange-panda allocation): neither arm names the labelled weakness in any round. In two of three repaired rounds the candidate raised, as bugs+impl (minor) and arch+quality (major), the same finding the #249 lens block had raised through docs+tests: that the repaired tests take their expected alias from the allocator's own output. The adjudicator rejected it both times: the stub records the argument herdr-child passed to herdr agent start, so the expectation is observed at the stub boundary, not derived from the allocator. Naming herdr-aliases.sh next to the stub led two finders to that conclusion; the baseline produced none of it.
  • Pair 4 (a Herdr stub that accepted an equal sequence production rejects): no finder in either arm names it in six bad rounds, with the stub and herdr-task-sync named side by side in the scope. The scope line that was written for this defect did not surface it.

The issue allows a zero-change result, and this is one. Candidate 1 of #577 is measured; candidates 2 (a test-evidence finder) and 3 (a stage rule) are not.
hits_prose: The table is the cross-arm adjudication: one agent per pair read all twelve rounds of that pair under opaque round ids, six from the #249 baseline and six new candidate rounds. The baseline's one false positive on pair 4 is lean-1 in repetition 3 of the repaired change: the regression check for equal sequences "has not been calibrated against the original defect". The #249 adjudicator, reading the same round, did not count it; this one did. The baseline rounds were therefore judged twice by different blind agents: 15 of 18 round verdicts are identical. The three differences are that false positive, and two finder-stage hits that the #249 adjudicator recorded on repaired rounds of pair 3 and this one did not; only the false positive changes a scored cell. That puts the adjudication noise at one scored cell in eighteen rounds.
limits:
• Three pairs, nine bad rounds per arm. A scope change that helps one category in ten would not show here. Pair 1 of the corpus was excluded for size, as in #249.
  • The baseline arm was not re-run: it is the 18 lean rounds of the #249 measurement, two days older than the candidate rounds. Same frozen commits, same profile, same revmux 0.2.7 and scratch config; the models behind opus and gpt-6.1-sol are the same identifiers but their service state two days apart is not controlled.
  • The adjudicator is a model (gpt-5.6-terra, high, one per pair). It saw the stage of each round, bad or repaired, which the false-positive question needs; it did not see the arm.
  • The production counterpart of the stubs in pairs 3 and 4 is the installed herdr binary, so the scope could name only its --help contract and its callers, not a source file with the rule. For pair 4 the rule the stub got wrong (equal sequence rejected) is not stated by herdr pane report-metadata --help either, so even a finder that read everything named had nothing to compare the stub against. That is a limit of the candidate, not only of the measurement.
  • The candidate rounds of pair 3 read more: 12.9M tokens per bad round against 10.8M, and 17.7 final findings against 19.3. The scope line changed what the finders read, not what they concluded about the labelled test.
next:
• Record the zero-change result on #577 and #249. The scope template and the managed lean profile stay as they are.
  • Two candidates on the #577 list remain unmeasured. The pair-4 limit above argues for a stage rule (candidate 3) or a finder brief (candidate 2) that asks, for a stub, where the rule it encodes is documented and what happens on the boundary value, rather than for more files to read.
  • Reuse of a baseline arm across measurements worked: the same 18 rounds judged twice by different adjudicators agreed on 15, and on every scored cell but one. A future measurement on these pairs can reuse them again and spend its rounds on the candidate.
